title: Height from an angle of elevation of 45 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.5 Quick check 1 (elevation 45, distance 20, height 20); tan 45 = 1, new distances
stem: From a point on horizontal ground {d|int} m from the foot of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is \(45^\circ\). What is the height of the tower, in metres?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(\tan 45^\circ=1\), so the height equals the horizontal distance and is {A|int} m.
steps.note: A equals d. Original d=20 gives height 20.

title: Height of a kite string at 30 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.5 Quick check 2 (string 50 m at 30 degrees, height 25); sin 30 = 1/2, new even string lengths
stem: A kite string of length {S|int} m makes a \(30^\circ\) angle with the horizontal ground. What is the height of the kite above the ground, in metres?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The height is the opposite side to \(30^\circ\), so it is \({S|int}\sin 30^\circ={S|int}\times 1/2={A|int}\).
steps.note: A is k and S is 2k. Original k=25 gives string 50 and height 25.

title: Horizontal distance from an angle of depression of 45 degrees
source: Theory IGCSE-15.5 Quick check 3 (depression 45, height 12, distance 12); tan 45 = 1, new heights
stem: From the top of a vertical cliff {h|int} m high, the angle of depression of a boat is \(45^\circ\). How far is the boat from the foot of the cliff, in metres?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The angle of depression from the horizontal equals the angle of elevation from the boat, which is \(45^\circ\). \(\tan 45^\circ=1\), so the horizontal distance equals the height and is {A|int} m.
steps.note: A equals h. Original h=12 gives distance 12.

title: Angle between a sloping edge and the base of a square pyramid

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2019), Question 4(d) only, including the labelled lengths DB=8 cm and PX=5 cm from the official diagram. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Parts 4(a) to 4(c) are omitted (unrelated surface area and similar cones).

stem:
This question is 0580/41/O/N/19 Question 4(d), taken from the official QP.

The diagram shows a pyramid with a square base \(ABCD\).
\(DB=8\) cm.
\(P\) is vertically above the centre, \(X\), of the base and \(PX=5\) cm.

Calculate the angle between \(PB\) and the base \(ABCD\).  [3]

steps.name: M
steps.text_tex: \(X\) is the midpoint of the diagonal \(DB\), so \(XB=4\) cm. The required angle is \(\angle PBX\), and \(\tan\angle PBX=5/4\).
steps.note: Official MS 4(d): M2 for tan = 5/4 oe; or M1 for recognition of angle PBX. Independent: XB = 8/2 = 4 and PX is perpendicular to the base.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The angle is \(\tan^{-1}(5/4)=51.340\ldots^\circ\), which is \(51.3^\circ\) to 3 significant figures.
steps.note: Official MS 4(d): 51.3 or 51.34... for 3 marks. Independent: arctan(1.25) = 51.34019175... degrees.
